name: update_position_limits
description: Adds a delta to two position variables, clamps each one between fixed lower and upper bounds, and stores a masked value in a flags variable. The delta comes from a global that is cleared just before it is used.

name: scale_input_values
description: Doubles two input word values and stores each result in its own global position variable.

name: return_halved_position_value
description: Returns one global position value shifted right by one bit, which halves it.

name: compare_and_reset_table
description: Scans a 12-byte table against a copy of itself 16 bytes ahead to find the first differing bit. When a qualifying difference is found it loads a global from the table and copies three shadow values; otherwise it clears the offset copy of the table.

name: translate_status_byte_to_flags
description: Calls a function through a pointer stored in a global, then rebuilds a status word by translating individual bits of a memory byte into fixed flag positions.

name: encode_direction_bits_from_flags
description: Builds a four-bit direction pattern from two pairs of flag bits in a global, keeping the upper word of the input register. It also sets a high bit when the global is non-negative.

name: encode_direction_bits_with_sign
description: Uses the same two flag-pair encoding as its sibling routine, but the high bit depends on the sign of a byte in a data register rather than on a global.

name: call_slot_if_above_one
description: Calls a function pointer stored at a fixed offset from a global value, but only when that value is greater than one.

name: call_alt_slot_above_one
description: Calls a different function pointer, at another fixed offset from the same global, under the same greater-than-one condition.

name: call_table_entry_or_fail
description: Calls two helper routines, then calls a function pointer read from a table. Returns that result, or minus one when it is zero.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Does no work and returns zero, so it acts as a no-op stub.

name: call_second_entry_if_nonzero
description: Calls two helper routines around a table function pointer. If that pointer returns a nonzero value, a second table entry is called with a passed-through register value.

name: call_entries_or_spin_forever
description: Calls a table entry, then either runs a helper and returns, or calls two more table entries and then spins forever in an empty loop.

name: call_entry_or_minus_one
description: Calls two helper routines, then a function pointer read from a table. Returns that result, or minus one when it is zero.

name: call_helpers_then_table_entry
description: Calls two helper routines, then a function pointer read from a table. Returns that result, or minus one when it is zero.

name: call_table_entry_between_helpers
description: Calls a helper, then a function pointer read from a fixed table offset, then another helper, and returns nothing.

name: call_read_table_entry
description: Calls a single function pointer stored at a fixed offset from a global base and returns, with no other work.

name: ensure_minimum_value_then_call
description: Sets a state global to one when it is below two, calls a helper, calls a table entry, and then sets the state global to one again.

name: wait_for_return_after_prompt
description: Polls a state variable and a flag until ready. If the key code is neither of two expected letters, it prints the disk prompt text, reads input until a carriage return, and then spins forever. The referenced text asks the user to unprotect the disk and press RETURN.

name: move_and_clear_quad_blocks
description: Copies four words per step from four source arrays into one contiguous destination, zeroing each source word after it is copied. It runs twenty steps per block over eighteen blocks.

name: copy_and_distribute_quad_blocks
description: Copies four words per step from one source array into four destination arrays, walking eighteen blocks of twenty steps. It does not clear the source.

name: stub_return_nothing
description: Returns immediately with no work, so it is a no-op stub.

name: poll_until_flag_bit_set
description: Calls a table function pointer to fetch a pointer. While that pointer's field has its upper bits set and its high bit is clear, it keeps fetching, retrying whenever a fetch returns null.

name: return_stack_argument
description: Returns an eight-byte value taken from the caller's stack argument, without changing it.

name: lock_handle_or_report_error
description: Calls a table function pointer and, when it returns zero, calls two helpers. Otherwise it saves the returned handle in a global and calls a second table entry. The referenced text reads error lock.

name: store_handle_if_sign_set
description: When a passed byte has its high bit set, calls a helper, saves a table call result in a global, calls two more table entries with a passed-through register, and stores a helper result in another global. Otherwise it returns at once.

name: lock_drive_for_small_index
description: When a passed byte is below two, gets a name through a helper, locks it through a table entry and saves the handle in a global. The referenced text contains the drive names DF0, DF1 and DH0.

name: call_helper_return_global
description: Calls a helper routine, then returns the byte value of a global.

name: store_handle_and_call_entries
description: Calls a helper, saves the result of a table function pointer in a global, calls that pointer again with a passed-through register, calls a second table entry, and stores a helper result in another global. The referenced text contains the drive names DF0, DF1 and DH0.

name: wait_for_flag_then_return
description: If a passed byte is below two, repeatedly calls two helpers while a state word is minus one, then returns the result of a further helper. Otherwise it returns the constant one hundred.

name: wait_for_flag_then_return
description: The same wait-then-return logic as its neighbours: while a state word is minus one it calls two helpers, then returns a further helper result, or one hundred when the input byte is not below two. Only this short body was recovered, although the routine is much larger.

name: wait_for_flag_then_return
description: If a passed byte is below two, repeatedly calls two helpers while a state word is minus one, then returns the result of a further helper. Otherwise it returns the constant one hundred.

name: lock_drive_handle_or_fail
description: Locks a drive name through a table entry. On failure it returns the all-ones 16-bit value; on success it saves the handle in a global, calls a second table entry and returns the result of a third.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_if_changed
description: When a chosen pointer differs from the current buffer pointer, saves a five-word record, overwrites it with fixed values, swaps two pointer globals and then restores the saved record. Two helper calls run around the swap.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_if_changed
description: When a chosen pointer differs from the current buffer pointer, saves a five-word record, overwrites it with fixed values, swaps two pointer globals and then restores the saved record. Two helper calls run around the swap.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_if_changed
description: When a chosen pointer differs from the current buffer pointer, saves a five-word record, overwrites it with fixed values, swaps two pointer globals and then restores the saved record. Two helper calls run around the swap.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_if_changed
description: When a chosen pointer differs from the current buffer pointer, saves a five-word record, overwrites it with fixed values, swaps two pointer globals and then restores the saved record. Two helper calls run around the swap.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_if_changed
description: When a chosen pointer differs from the current buffer pointer, saves a five-word record, overwrites it with fixed values, swaps two pointer globals and then restores the saved record. Two helper calls run around the swap.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_if_changed
description: When a chosen pointer differs from the current buffer pointer, saves a five-word record, overwrites it with fixed values, swaps two pointer globals and then restores the saved record. Two helper calls run around the swap.

name: swap_buffer_pointers_on_mismatch
description: When a passed value differs from a stored value, saves a five-word record, overwrites it with fixed values, swaps two pointer globals, restores the record and calls two helpers.

name: shift_buffer_window_records
description: Walks a buffer window by a count taken from a global, swapping two buffer pointers and rewriting a five-word record with values shifted by a computed amount. It then runs a fixed loop, resets the window values to fixed numbers and restores the saved state.

name: shift_record_by_scaled_offset
description: Derives an offset by negating a global and shifting it right by three bits, adds that offset to five consecutive longwords of a record, and then calls a helper.

name: reset_window_record_defaults
description: Overwrites a five-word global record with fixed values, namely zero, zero, 319, 199 and 80, then calls a helper.

name: reset_window_record_defaults
description: Overwrites a five-word global record with fixed values, namely zero, zero, 319, 199 and 80, then calls a helper.

name: reset_window_record_defaults
description: Overwrites a five-word global record with fixed values, namely zero, zero, 319, 199 and 80, then calls a helper.

name: write_block_header_from_pointer
description: Calls a helper to obtain a block pointer. When the pointer is null it clears a global; otherwise it computes a row size from a structure field, derives sequential offsets and sizes from globals, and writes a size marker, a fixed word and two differences into the block header.

name: write_block_header_from_argument
description: Performs the same block header setup as its neighbour without the null check, then returns the stack argument it was given.

name: allocate_block_from_top_pool
description: Computes a padded block size from a requested size and subtracts it from a top-of-pool global. If the new position stays above a limit, it stores the size there and returns an address eight bytes past the block start; otherwise it returns null.

name: allocate_block_from_top_pool
description: Computes a padded block size from a requested size and subtracts it from a top-of-pool global. If the new position stays above a limit, it stores the size there and returns an address eight bytes past the block start; otherwise it returns null.

name: allocate_block_from_top_pool
description: Computes a padded block size from a requested size and subtracts it from a top-of-pool global. If the new position stays above a limit, it stores the size there and returns an address eight bytes past the block start; otherwise it returns null.

name: allocate_block_from_top_pool
description: Computes a padded block size from a requested size and subtracts it from a top-of-pool global. If the new position stays above a limit, it stores the size there and returns an address eight bytes past the block start; otherwise it returns null.

name: allocate_block_from_top_pool
description: Computes a padded block size from a requested size and subtracts it from a top-of-pool global. If the new position stays above a limit, it stores the size there and returns an address eight bytes past the block start; otherwise it returns null.

name: allocate_block_from_top_pool
description: Computes a padded block size from a requested size and subtracts it from a top-of-pool global. If the new position stays above a limit, it stores the size there and returns an address eight bytes past the block start; otherwise it returns null.

name: return_stack_longword
description: Returns the four-byte value passed on the stack, unchanged.

name: check_word_in_exclusive_range
description: Returns zero when a passed word lies strictly inside a fixed exclusive window, and the all-ones 16-bit value otherwise.

name: return_all_ones_word
description: Returns the all-ones 16-bit value without any other work.

name: stub_return_nothing
description: Returns immediately with no work, so it is a no-op stub.

name: increment_global_if_nonzero
description: Calls a helper, and when the returned word is nonzero adds two hundred thousand to a global counter.

name: call_helper_return_entry_registers
description: Calls a helper and then returns the two 32-bit data-register values it was entered with.

name: call_helper_and_return
description: Calls a single helper routine and returns with no other work.

name: clip_and_merge_shifted_planes
description: Clips a rectangle against bounds held in globals, then for up to sixteen rows merges four source bit-plane words, shifted by a sub-word offset, into four destination planes under a mask. When a status flag is set it clears a group of state longwords first.

name: copy_four_plane_rows_strided
description: Copies rows of four bit-plane words from a source buffer into the current destination plane set, advancing by fixed strides. A flag controls whether an extra group of source words is skipped on each row.

name: start_blitter_copy_job
description: Computes a plane offset from clip values, loads the blitter masks, modulo and control values into globals, and starts a sized blit after waiting for the blitter to be idle. Further waits in the same routine guard the remaining register writes.

name: run_blitter_row_loop
description: Loads blitter masks and a control word, then loops once per row. Before each row it waits for the blitter to be idle, starts a sized blit with advancing source and destination offsets, and moves to the next row.

name: copy_four_plane_block_rows
description: When the row count is above 199 and not exactly 320, it delegates to a helper and returns that result. Otherwise it copies a block row by row from one set of four plane pointers into another, advancing both by a stride after each row.

name: start_blitter_block_copy
description: Configures the blitter with a control word, full masks and a source-to-destination offset taken from a plane pointer, waits for it to be idle, then starts a blit sized by the block height and width.

name: start_blit_unless_flagged
description: When neither of two status bits is set, loads blitter masks and a control value chosen by a test, waits for the blitter and starts a blit from a source pointer. Otherwise it stores a computed offset in a global.

name: clip_and_translate_block_bytes
description: Clips a block's bounds against limits, then copies bytes from a source into a destination buffer through a lookup table indexed by byte value. The row order is swapped in one branch, selected by a flag.

name: clip_and_blit_sprite_record
description: Clips a sprite record against window limits and returns early when it lies outside. Otherwise it stores clip bounds in globals, chooses an edge mask and blit path from the record's type byte, and returns a clipped value.

name: clip_and_draw_sprite_record
description: Clips a sprite record against the window and returns early when it is outside. Otherwise it stores clip bounds, then picks an edge mask and blit path from the type byte and starts the blitter, with a simpler path for some types.

name: store_status_for_matched_handler
description: When a global is zero and an address register matches one of four known handler pointers, stores the global into that handler's second word and calls a helper. Otherwise it returns without work.

name: setup_audio_channel_playback
description: Calls a system routine, then programs one audio channel's pointer, length, period and volume registers, capping the volume at 100. It records the channel in a global and calls another table entry to start it.

name: stop_audio_channel_if_active
description: When a channel's status byte has its high bit set, clears that status. When a secondary flag is set, it returns early unless a countdown word has reached zero. It then sets the channel's bit in a global mask.

name: service_flagged_channel_helpers
description: Checks four flag bits in a global and calls a helper for each one that is set, then writes a fixed constant to the global. The helpers are not identified in the pseudo-code.

name: advance_audio_channel_countdown
description: Decrements a countdown word for an audio channel. When it reaches zero, it clears the channel's status and record fields, copies a long value within the record, zeroes the channel volume and sets its bit in a global. Otherwise it writes the remaining value to the channel volume register.

name: copy_word_to_channel_volume
description: Copies a word from a record at a fixed offset into the audio volume register selected by a channel index.

name: call_four_helpers_in_order
description: Calls four helper routines in sequence and returns.

name: call_helper_return_entry_registers
description: Calls a helper and then returns the two 32-bit data-register values it was entered with.

name: install_handler_if_flag_set
description: When a flag word is nonzero, loads a stored handler address into the dispatch variable and sets a companion byte to one. Otherwise it calls a helper.

name: store_global_as_handler_address
description: Copies a global value, as an unsigned word, into a stored handler-address variable and returns.

name: store_and_scale_global
description: Copies a global value into one variable and stores a second variable holding that value multiplied by six and shifted right by five bits.

name: clear_audio_volumes_if_flagged
description: Returns when a flag byte is clear. If a second value is zero it calls a helper instead; otherwise it zeroes the volume registers of all four audio channels.

name: reset_audio_state_block
description: Optionally calls a helper, then zeroes a 32-entry table of longword targets, saves the state word, sets state globals, clears two audio volume registers and clears several word fields.

name: reset_audio_state_block
description: Optionally calls a helper, then zeroes a 32-entry table of longword targets, saves the state word, sets state globals, clears two audio volume registers and clears several word fields.

name: reset_audio_state_block_flagged
description: When a flag byte is set, calls a helper first. It then performs the same table zeroing and state update as its sibling routine, and finally sets the flag byte to one.

name: reset_audio_state_block
description: Optionally calls a helper, then zeroes a 32-entry table of longword targets, saves the state word, sets state globals, clears two audio volume registers and clears several word fields.

name: reset_audio_state_block
description: Optionally calls a helper, then zeroes a 32-entry table of longword targets, saves the state word, sets state globals, clears two audio volume registers and clears several word fields.

name: silence_audio_channels_and_reset
description: Zeroes the volume registers of all four audio channels, writes a fixed value into one global, and clears a longword table pointer and a flag byte.

name: update_channel_volumes_from_envelope
description: Decrements a timer and derives a volume scale from a ratio, or from a second timer when the first is idle. It then writes each audio channel's volume register from a stored level multiplied by that scale, but only for channels whose flag word is zero.

name: advance_audio_sequence_step
description: Advances a 128-entry ring position when a flag is set. At the end of a pass it resets the step, calls several helpers and programs a timer register. Otherwise it clears all four audio volume registers and resets the state globals.

name: store_pending_audio_values
description: Copies a saved word into a global and writes a fixed bit mask into another global.

name: load_audio_channel_registers
description: For each audio channel whose flag is zero, copies a saved pointer and length into that channel's location and length registers. It then writes a fixed mask into two global control words.

name: process_channel_sequence_command
description: Loads an event from a per-channel record and, when its index is nonzero, sets the sample pointer, length and period from a table. It then handles the record's command code: zero does nothing, while other codes set a flag, a control bit, a volume clamped at 64, or a scaled volume.

name: process_channel_command_at_offset
description: Updates a channel record's period from a supplied offset and a table value, then handles the command code as the sibling routine does, setting a flag, a control bit, a clamped volume or a scaled volume.

name: apply_channel_command_nibble
description: Reads a channel's control word and applies its command code. Zero does nothing; other codes set a flag, a control bit, a clamped volume, or leave the state unchanged.

name: step_channel_period_toward_target
description: Stores the channel's current period and compares it with its target. When they match it clears the working period and stops; when the period is lower it sets a direction flag. It then applies the record's command code.

name: clear_channel_slide_value
description: Clears a 16-bit slide field in a channel record.

name: slide_channel_period_toward_target
description: Applies a pending slide amount to a channel's period, moving it up or down by direction and clamping it at the target. When the target is reached it clears the target, and it writes the period register when the channel's flag word is zero.

name: slide_channel_period_by_step
description: Moves a channel's period toward its target by a supplied step, rising or falling by direction and clamping at the target. When the target is reached it clears the target, and it writes the period register when the channel's flag word is zero.

name: lower_channel_period_by_step
description: Subtracts a supplied step from a channel's period. When the result reaches its target it clamps to the target and clears it. The period register is written when the channel's flag word is zero.

name: apply_table_modulated_period
description: Stores a new depth value when one is supplied, then computes an offset from a table indexed by a phase field and scales it by the depth. The offset is negated when a sign bit is set, added to the channel's base period when its flag word is zero, and the phase is advanced.

name: advance_table_modulated_period
description: Computes the same table-modulated period offset as its neighbour without storing a new depth. It writes the result to the period register when the flag word is zero, then advances the phase field.

name: set_period_from_difference
description: Writes the difference between two supplied words to the channel's period register when its flag word is zero, then advances the phase field.

name: select_period_from_mode_table
description: When a mode byte is nonzero, walks a table until a value is not greater than the channel's period, then writes the entry chosen by a nibble of a parameter to the period register when the flag word is zero. When the mode byte is zero it writes the base period instead.

name: walk_period_table_to_register
description: Walks a table until a value is not greater than the channel's period, then writes the entry selected by a parameter nibble to the period register when the flag word is zero.

name: write_base_period_if_unflagged
description: Writes the base period to the period register when the channel's flag word is zero.

name: dispatch_effect_if_flag_clear
description: Returns the incoming value unchanged when the channel's flag word is nonzero. Otherwise it reads the effect code in the low nibble of a control word and dispatches on it, as the sibling dispatcher does.

name: dispatch_channel_effect_code
description: Dispatches the effect code in the low nibble of a control word. Code four applies a table-modulated period offset and advances the phase, code three runs a slide step that clamps to a target, and codes five and six call helpers. The pseudo-code is cut off, so the remaining cases are not described.

name: lower_period_with_floor
description: Subtracts a parameter byte from the channel's period, clamps the result to a floor of 113, and writes it to the period register when the flag word is zero.

name: raise_period_with_ceiling
description: Adds a parameter byte to the channel's period, clamps the result to a ceiling of 856, and writes it to the period register when the flag word is zero.

name: adjust_channel_volume_level
description: Calls a helper first, then adjusts a channel volume level by a nibble from a parameter. The high nibble adds to the level with a cap of 64, and the low nibble subtracts with a floor of zero. The level is stored and a scaled volume is written when the flag word is zero.

name: adjust_channel_volume_level
description: Calls a helper first, then adjusts a channel volume level by a nibble from a parameter. The high nibble adds to the level with a cap of 64, and the low nibble subtracts with a floor of zero. The level is stored and a scaled volume is written when the flag word is zero.

name: decrease_channel_volume_level
description: Subtracts the low nibble of a parameter from the channel's volume level, floored at zero, stores the level and writes a scaled volume to the volume register when the flag word is zero.

name: apply_command_nibble_without_load
description: Applies the command code in the low nibble of a channel's control byte. Zero does nothing; one code sets a control bit from a parameter, another sets a flag, another stores a volume clamped at 64, another stores a scaled level, and another sets a flag and a counter.

name: copy_parameter_bit_to_status
description: Sets bit one of a global status word from bit zero of a parameter byte, leaving the other bits unchanged.

name: set_channel_pending_flag
description: Sets a pending flag byte in a channel record to one.

name: set_flag_and_countdown_byte
description: Sets a flag byte in a channel record to one and stores one less than a parameter byte in a companion countdown byte.

name: set_channel_volume_clamped
description: Clamps a parameter byte to a maximum of 64, stores it as the channel's level and writes a scaled volume to the volume register when the flag word is zero.

name: set_scaled_level_byte
description: Caps a parameter byte at 31, multiplies it by a global scale, shifts the product right by five bits and stores the result in a channel byte.

name: copy_longwords_to_low_memory
description: Copies consecutive longwords upward from a source address into a destination until the source reaches a fixed end address, then returns. The routine does nothing else.

name: patch_byte_when_patterns_match
description: Returns the byte at the address register after a conditional write. When that byte is zero and neighbouring bytes match one of two fixed patterns, it writes a fixed byte value at a fixed offset.

name: patch_byte_when_pattern_matches
description: When neighbouring bytes at fixed offsets match a fixed pattern, writes one fixed byte value at a fixed offset, then returns the byte at the address register.

name: initialise_record_with_dos_tag
description: Writes fixed values into a record: zeros in the first two longwords and in two later longwords, the numbers 82 and 10000 in two others, and the ASCII bytes of DOS followed by a zero byte in another. It returns the all-ones longword.
